dedupe_keys.name: chime covid 19 hospital impact model for epidemics

description: CHIME (COVID-19 Hospital Impact Model for Epidemics) helps hospitals and public health officials understand hospital capacity needs during an epidemic. From a regional population, the current number of hospitalised patients and an assumed doubling time or level of social distancing, it runs a standard SIR (susceptible, infected, recovered) model and converts infections into daily new and running totals (census) of inpatient hospitalisations, ICU admissions and patients requiring ventilation, using user-set hospitalisation rates, lengths of stay and the hospital's market share. Predictive Healthcare at Penn Medicine created it in March 2020 and Code for Philly took over development; the README states that epidemiologists at the Perelman School of Medicine validated the model. Coverage is any hospital or health region the user parameterises; resolution is one region and one day. It is Python code on GitHub (latest tag v1.1.5) with a Streamlit web application that still answers at penn-chime.phl.io, and user and developer documentation. Licence: MIT, free. Caveats: the SIR structure is deliberately simple and designed for COVID-19; development stopped after 2020, so it is stale and parameters must be updated by the user. Simulation uses: surge capacity planning of hospital beds, ICUs and ventilators, and emergency response to a pandemic. Related: COVID-19 Scenarios and Covasim model the same hospital demand with richer epidemic dynamics (catalogued as model-covid19-scenarios and model-covasim).
